text:
maya: Hi team — customer reports websocket streaming stops right before final tokens (client never gets final chunk / no "[DONE]" frame). They hit it consistently on a single route behind a corporate proxy. Customer provided request IDs: rq_1794218001, rq_1794218023, rq_1794218056. They say it worked earlier today and started failing ~2026-03-15 14:02 UTC.

alex: Thanks @maya. Can you confirm model + region + any proxy details they gave? Also ask them for a minimal repro (wscat or curl fallback) and a full nginx/forward-proxy header dump if possible.

maya: Model: redwood-7b-instruct, region: us-west-2, client network: corporate-proxy (Squid) -> AWS ALB. They captured a short websocket session with timestamps and attached to the ticket (I have the file locally). I asked them to try wscat; they said it still reproduces.

ingrid: If they can share a small session capture that would be ideal. In the meantime, try reproducing from our office with the same model/flags. Typical root causes: proxy buffering or HTTP/2 flow control with ALB/nginx refusing to flush short frames. Can @maya paste a minimal repro command to ask the customer to run (both ws + SSE fallback)?

maya: Pasting suggested repro for customer (asked them to run both):
```
# websocket (wscat)
# open WS, then send JSON on a single line
wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-7b-instruct" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
> {"prompt":"Summarize: hello","max_tokens":60,"stream":true}

# SSE fallback with curl (keeps connection open, --no-buffer helps)
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"Summarize: hello","max_tokens":60,"stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
```

alex: Good. Also ask them to run `curl --http1.1` to rule out HTTP/2 server->proxy issues: `curl --http1.1 -N ...`

kevin: If they can share one of the request IDs we can pull router/nginx logs for that timespan. @maya you gave rq_1794218001 etc — I'll pull logs for +/- 2 minutes around the timestamp. Also we should request a pcap from them if corporate policy allows.

support-bot: Debug bundle helper — to collect a debug bundle for a Redwood request run: `redwood-support collect --request rq_1794218001 --include nginx,router,proxy-headers,kernel-trace` then upload the tar to the secure bucket and paste the link. If customer cannot run our helper, ask for: `curl -v` stdout, nginx access/error for the time window, and a `sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/stream.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443` capture.

ingrid: From our side I tried a quick repro from a laptop using wscat and a small local nginx reverse-proxy configured with buffering on. I saw identical behavior when nginx had `proxy_buffering on` and `proxy_http_version 1.1` — last chunk stayed in buffer until the connection closed. Sample router log around rq_1794218001: 
```
2026-03-15T14:02:07Z router[web-01] INFO request=rq_1794218001 bytes_sent=1024 state=streaming
2026-03-15T14:02:09Z router[web-01] WARN request=rq_1794218001 proxy_flush=delayed
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z router[web-01] INFO request=rq_1794218001 connection_closed_by_client
```
Shows flush got delayed and client closed. Could be a proxy coalescing small writes.

maya: Sent the repro + debug-bundle instructions to the customer. They replied with `curl -v` trace and said their proxy is Squid 4.15 and they cannot run tcpdump because of IT policy, but can share the proxy access logs and the `curl -v` output. They also tried `curl --http1.1` and said that made the symptoms intermittent (sometimes works).

alex: That strongly points at HTTP/2 or proxy buffering. Quick mitigation we can ask them to try: 1) use `--http1.1` in client, 2) set `Connection: keep-alive` vs `Connection: close` toggle on proxy (if they can), 3) for websockets, use a small periodic noop to keep the pipeline busy (not ideal). We'll need to escalate to runtime if customer can't change proxy.

kevin: I've pulled our side logs for rq_1794218001 -> there were no 5xx or internal errors. Router sent chunks as small frames, final frame was emitted by runtime at 14:02:11Z. No sign of server abort. Suggest we ask the customer to grep their proxy logs for the request timestamp and check for `TCP_FIN` or `RST` shortly after 14:02:11Z.

ingrid: Ops checklist for escalation if customer cannot change proxy: 1) confirm exact proxy product/version + config (http2, buffering), 2) try reproducing from a similarly configured Squid instance, 3) capture a minimal pcap if possible, 4) test SSE (curl) vs WS (wscat) differences. I've added a small runtime experiment to toggle `prefer_chunked_flush=true` for a single canary host to see if flushing policy affects this.

maya: Plan -> collect customer curl -v + proxy access logs for the time window, ask them to run the wscat + curl --http1.1 tests, and provide any policy blocking tcpdump. If they can't produce pcap we'll attempt a runtime canary change and sync back. I'll update the ticket and paste the uploaded logs here when I have them. :thumbsup:
